nodes.name: Webhook: Ingest Batch
nodes.notes: POST {batch_id, source?, records:[...]}. Replies once, after every record has been handled.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. The record schema (SCHEMA_JSON), service URLs, limits. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Plan Batch
nodes.notes: Checks auth (optional), CONFIG and the batch envelope (batch_id, records array, size limit). Nothing is validated per record here; that is the next node.

nodes.name: Validate Records
nodes.notes: THE ENGINE (do not edit). Validates and cleans every record against SCHEMA_JSON in one pass; nothing is loaded yet. One bad record never affects another. Dates must be real ISO dates; the first record with an id wins and later copies are rejected with a reason. To add your own rules, edit the Custom Rules node instead.

nodes.name: Custom Rules
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. Client-specific logic goes here: transforms (change a record), rules (reject a record with a reason) and payload (what is sent). Only edit between the EDIT lines. Enforce Rules checks the result afterwards.

nodes.name: Enforce Rules
nodes.notes: THE GUARD (do not edit). Re-checks what Custom Rules produced: every record accounted for exactly once, ids unchanged, payload a JSON object. A broken Custom Rules node gives a clear 500 instead of loading anything.

nodes.name: Respond Early
nodes.notes: Replies to batches that stop early: 400 (bad batch), 401, 500 (bad CONFIG).

nodes.name: Load Records
nodes.notes: THE LOADER. Loads valid records one at a time and keeps state between them, which n8n's normal node-by-node flow cannot: retries with back-off on transient failures, a destination that refuses a record (4xx) is a data problem not an outage, N failures in a row (or the shared breaker opening) stops the rest of the batch, and a time budget keeps the caller from waiting forever. Each record carries an idempotency key batch_id:id.

nodes.name: Dead Letter Items
nodes.notes: Collects everything that was not loaded, with the original record, for ONE dead-letter call.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { batch_id: $json.batch_id, source: $json.source, received_at: new Date().toISOString(), items: $json.dl_items } }}

nodes.name: Save Dead Letters
nodes.notes: POST /dead-letters {batch_id, source, received_at, items:[{row, record_id, status, failure_type, reasons, record}]} -> 2xx. One call per batch (the original made one per record and ignored failures).

nodes.name: Save Dead Letters Transient?
nodes.notes: One retry for a transient failure.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { batch_id: $('Dead Letter Items').first().json.batch_id, source: $('Dead Letter Items').first().json.source, received_at: new Date().toISOString(), items: $('Dead Letter Items').first().json.dl_items } }}

nodes.name: Save Dead Letters (retry)
nodes.notes: The one retry.

nodes.name: Build Response
nodes.notes: The one response: per-record outcome (without echoing the data back), counts, whether the dead letters were saved, and what the breaker did. status = completed | partial | failed (HTTP stays 200: the batch was processed). Ops is alerted only for operational trouble (load failures, skips, lost dead letters), never for bad source data.

nodes.name: Respond Batch
nodes.notes: The single reply for a processed batch.

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. One Slack message per problem; nothing if Slack is not configured.

nodes.name: Send Slack Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed alert is ignored on purpose.

nodes.name: Webhook: Replay
nodes.notes: POST {ids? | batch_id? , failure_type?, limit?} with header x-replay-token. Re-runs open dead letters through the same validation and load. Off (403) unless CONFIG.REPLAY_ENABLED is true.

nodes.name: Is Replay?
nodes.notes: Both webhooks share the one CONFIG node, then split here.

nodes.name: Plan Replay
nodes.notes: Order: switch (403), settings (500), token (401), CONFIG (500), body (400). Its own token (x-replay-token), separate from the ingest token.

nodes.name: Claim Dead Letters
nodes.notes: Lists the open dead letters (or fetches the ids you gave), re-checks them itself, and CLAIMS each through the store's atomic claim call. Only claimed records are run. They then go through the same validation, rules and loader as a normal batch, under the idempotency key of their original batch.

nodes.name: Settle Replay
nodes.notes: After a replay: tells the dead-letter store what happened to each record (loaded = resolved; failed = stays open with the new reason and one more attempt; skipped by the breaker = released, not counted as an attempt). A record that loaded but could not be marked resolved is listed and reported to ops (it will be replayed again, which is safe because of the idempotency key).

parameters.content:
## Data Validation ETL Pipeline
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 03-data-validation-etl-mock-server.js`, port 4900): destination, circuit breaker, dead-letter store, Slack stand-in.
2. Open **CONFIG**: edit `SCHEMA_JSON` (the fields your records must have; the default is id, email, amount, currency, created_at), `ID_FIELD`, the service URLs, optional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` and `ETL_AUTH_TOKEN`.
3. Activate. Send `POST /webhook/etl/ingest` with `{"batch_id":"b-1","source":"partner-a","records":[...]}`.

**Each batch:** validate the envelope -> validate and clean every record -> load the valid ones one at a time (retries, breaker, time budget) -> save everything that failed to the dead-letter store (one call) -> reply with per-record results -> alert ops about operational trouble only.
